entries.gave: Read the Cut, docs/product-vision.md as it stands, round 4 Made, and the one More kept (refactor-doc N6 on KR1.1). Its people: the developers of invoicer, who build for two roles, the accounting team printing each client invoice at its own rate without a developer, and the developers who call the library and install the command once.
Read product-vision best-practice.md with template.md, and refactor-doc best-practice.md, to their end before any change.
Job from the goal: invoicer turns invoice lines into a right invoice for those who print it or call it; taken as the Cut N1 decisions give it.
Roles named by the part of the job: the accounting team prints invoices; the developers call the library from their own code.
Printing needs the one install a developer does; N1 decision 1 puts the install in the Developer role.
No role left unclear: the person settled both roles in the N1 decisions; nothing to ask.
Library use and install would split by this practice, but N1 decision 2 keeps one Developer role as the person chose; no split.
The accounting team and the developers count different results as done; no merge.
Two roles, so neither is named user.
O1 has the accounting team as subject, O2 and O3 the developers, as N2 decision 0 words them.
Each objective ends in the role own work: billing each client what they owe; their own code giving the same results; a command never set up again. Unchanged from round 4, judged good.
Three distinct ends, each reachable without the others: O1, O2, O3 kept.

Tasks: O1 from starting a client invoice to holding it printed; O2 from updating invoicer to their own code giving its results; O3 from starting the install to the command running for the accounting team.
First key results count the share that fails; KR1.1 takes the person wording from N4 decision 1: the share of printed invoices that are wrong or needed a developer help.
Second key results: KR1.2 and KR3.2 time with the role own time included; KR2.2 counts the edits, as update time depends on things outside invoicer. Unchanged.
Each key result ends with Lower is better.
Ranking per N4 decision 0: the template line with KR2.1, KR1.1 and KR3.1 come first; per decision 2 the line does not rank KR1.2, KR2.2 and KR3.2 among themselves, the person departure.
No targets; the template sentence on Goodhart law stays.
Pieces of work from the Cut: print from invoice lines, name bad lines, rate set at each print, one rounding of tax in the library, the one install.
Printing, bad lines and rate serve O1; the one rounding serves O2; the install serves O3, per N5 decision 0.
Each pair of objectives has a piece serving one without the other; no merge.
No piece names more than one objective after N5 decision 0; nothing to split.
Every piece serves an objective; nothing to ask.
The person gave the one way and its ideas, in N6 decision 0; not asked again.
One way: invoicer turns invoice lines into an invoice whose totals are right without anyone redoing the math.
The three ideas as the person worded them, each with what it gives toward O1 or O2.
Moments: the install, opening the invoice lines, setting the rate, printing, a bad line, an update of invoicer under their own code.
Each moment has its idea but the install, which takes no idea by the person choice in N6 decision 0; nothing proposed.
No idea proposed, so none put to the person.
Three ideas, each one the way stands on; none moved or dropped.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end: Roles says who comes, Objectives and key results what each achieves and how it is measured, Concept the one way and its ideas.
Readers: the developers of invoicer, who decide what to build and judge each change by the vision.
The developers know Python and invoicer library; they come to learn whom it serves, how a change is judged, and the way every choice leans.
The three template sections each hold one topic; no split.
Each looked-for item has its own heading or list item: roles, O and KR ids, ideas.
Roles, objectives and ideas are items in no order, bulleted; the ranking line and its reason stay prose in the template form.
Readers own words: the goal (invoice lines, spreadsheet, tax rate) and the person words in the Cut (their own code, printed invoices, a developer help).
KR1.1 counts printed invoices, the person word, in place of print tasks, which no reader uses; this makes the More kept good.
Facts stated twice: none; the source of the lines and the rate at each print live only in the Concept.
Each fact has its one place, as N3 decision 0 sets: Roles for who, Concept for the lines and the rate.
No fact stated two different ways; nothing to ask.
Names: accounting team, developers, invoice lines, their own code, the command, the library, invoicer; printed invoices replaces print tasks.
No thing has two names; invoice lines and their own code kept, per N3 decision 0.
No name refers to two things.

Decided: every Cut decision taken as it stands; KR1.1 takes the person wording; the ranking line names KR2.1, KR1.1 and KR3.1 come first; the four departures stay. Settled without asking: come in place of comes, as three key results are its subject. Nothing open.
